title.zh: 风险厌恶与确定性等价：为什么买平均亏钱的保险
title.en: Risk aversion and the certainty equivalent: why buy insurance that loses on average

description.zh: 怕风险的人愿意为确定多付钱，最多肯付的保费减去平均损失就是风险溢价。
description.en: A risk-averse person pays extra for certainty; the most they would pay minus the expected loss is the risk premium.

zh: 保险明明亏钱为什么还买

title.en: The market for lemons and adverse selection

description.zh: 买家看不清质量只能按平均出价，好货退出，平均变差，市场一轮轮萎缩。
description.en: Buyers who cannot see quality offer the average price; good goods withdraw, the average falls and the market shrinks round by round.

zh: 二手车市场为什么烂车多

title.zh: 死亡螺旋、强制参保与核保

description.zh: 按平均定价赶走最健康的人，保费越涨越高；强制、补贴或按体检分档能打断它。
description.en: Average pricing drives out the healthiest and premiums climb; mandates, subsidies or underwriting classes can break the spiral.

zh: 为什么体检后保费不同
医保为什么要连续参保

description.zh: 全保贵、带免赔额便宜，两类人各选一份，用选择说出自己的风险；罗斯柴尔德—斯蒂格利茨模型。
description.en: Full cover at a high price and a cheap plan with a deductible let each risk type reveal itself by its choice: the Rothschild–Stiglitz model.

zh: 保险公司为什么要免赔额
罗斯柴尔德斯蒂格利茨

title.zh: 信号：文凭、保修、口碑与花钱证明自己
title.en: Signalling: diplomas, warranties, reputation and costly proof

description.zh: 知道得多的一方做一件冒充者做不起的事来证明自己——文凭、保修、品牌、认证、口碑；只要代价因人而异，哪怕这件事本身没用也能传递信息（斯宾塞模型）。
description.en: The better-informed side proves itself by doing something too costly to fake: diplomas, warranties, brands, certification, reputation. If the cost differs by type, even a useless act carries information (Spence).

title.zh: 道德风险、自付比例与委托—代理

description.zh: 一方的行为另一方看不见、而后果有人兜底时，人会少小心、多冒险——保险、雇佣、存款保险、救助都是；办法是让行动者自担一部分后果（委托—代理问题）。
description.en: When one side cannot see the other's actions and someone else bears the consequences, people take less care and more risk, in insurance, employment, deposit insurance and bail-outs alike; the remedy is making the actor bear part of the outcome (the principal–agent problem).

title.zh: 信贷配给：银行为什么不随便放贷
title.en: Credit rationing: why banks refuse rather than raise rates

description.zh: 高利率先赶走稳当的借款人，银行的期望回报会在某个利率后下降，于是宁可拒贷；斯蒂格利茨—韦斯模型。
description.en: High rates drive out safe borrowers first, so the bank's expected return can fall beyond some rate and it rations credit instead: Stiglitz–Weiss.

zh: 银行为什么不随便放贷

title.en: Where a credit score comes from

description.zh: 评分卡把过去的还款记录变成违约概率和分数，银行再定门槛；没有记录本身也是信息。
description.en: A scorecard turns your repayment history into a default probability and a score, and the bank sets a cutoff; a thin file is information too.

title.zh: 大数据定价、基因信息与参保规则的前沿
title.en: Data-driven pricing, genetic information and enrolment rules: the frontier

description.zh: 看得越清螺旋越难转、高风险者越难投保：大数据杀熟条款、欧盟 AI 法、GINA、医保断保等待期。
description.en: Seeing more stops spirals but prices out high risks: China's anti-price-discrimination rule, the EU AI Act, GINA and enrolment waiting periods.

label.en: Expected loss is the starting point

reason.zh: 第 1 章从期望损失出发，说明风险厌恶的人愿意为确定多付多少，并链到《期望》第 4 步。
reason.en: Chapter 1 starts from the expected loss and shows how much more a risk-averse person pays for certainty; it links step 4 of the expected-value lesson.

reason.zh: 第 1 章把买保险的溢价和投资里的风险溢价放在一起看：都是为不确定要的补偿，并链到风险与回报一课。
reason.en: Chapter 1 puts the insurance mark-up beside the investment risk premium, both a price for bearing uncertainty, and links the risk-and-return lesson.

reason.zh: 第 4 章里每个人对保险的出价，就是第 1 章的模型算出的最高保费。
reason.en: In chapter 4 each person’s bid for insurance is the maximum premium from chapter 1’s model.

label.en: When people choose whether to join

reason.zh: 第 2 章摘要风险池化后指出：如果投保人自己决定进出、又比保险公司更清楚自己的风险，池子就会变；第 3 章用二手车讲这件事。
reason.en: Chapter 2 summarises pooling and notes the pool changes if people choose to join and know their risk better than the insurer; chapter 3 tells that story with used cars.

reason.zh: 第 3 章说柠檬市场是一种市场失灵：每个人都做对自己合理的事，本来人人想做的交易却做不成，并链到《稀缺会搬家》第 6 章。
reason.en: Chapter 3 calls the lemons market a market failure: everyone acts sensibly, yet trades everyone wanted do not happen; it links chapter 6 of scarcity-moves.

reason.zh: 第 3 章把信息不对称和外部性对照：后者是成本甩给了别人，前者是一方看不清另一方。
reason.en: Chapter 3 contrasts hidden information with externalities: there a cost lands on others, here one side cannot see the other.

reason.zh: 第 4 章把第 3 章的二手车换成投保的人：低风险者先退出，保费上涨，再赶走下一批。
reason.en: Chapter 4 swaps chapter 3’s cars for policyholders: low risks leave first, the premium rises and drives out the next group.

label.en: A pool of high risks only

reason.zh: 第 4 章接着《风险池化与保险》第 4 步“为什么只有高风险的人留在保险里”，用 1,000 人的模型把螺旋走完。
reason.en: Chapter 4 continues step 4 of the risk-pooling lesson, on why only high risks stay insured, and runs the spiral with 1,000 people.

reason.zh: 第 4 章：在不知道自己健不健康之前选规则，风险厌恶的人会愿意选“一个价都参加”，等于给“生下来就是高风险”买保险。
reason.en: Chapter 4: choosing rules before knowing one’s health, a risk-averse person would accept one price for everyone, insuring against being born a high risk.

reason.zh: 第 5 章：只卖一种按平均定价的全保就会走上第 4 章的螺旋；免赔额菜单让低风险者自己选出来。
reason.en: Chapter 5: one full-cover contract at the average price leads to chapter 4’s spiral; a deductible menu lets the low risks sort themselves out.

reason.zh: 第 5 章：设计一张菜单，让每个人选了对自己最好的一项时正好说出真话，这类问题叫机制设计，拍卖是最有名的例子。
reason.en: Chapter 5: designing a menu so that each person’s best choice tells the truth is mechanism design, of which auctions are the best-known case.

label.en: The informed side pays to prove it

reason.zh: 第 3 章末尾把保修、检测报告、口碑列为柠檬市场的修补；第 6 章讲其中的信号：冒充太贵，信号才可信。
reason.en: Chapter 3 lists warranties, inspections and reputation as repairs for the lemons market; chapter 6 treats signals, credible because faking them costs too much.

label.zh: 雇主做一次贝叶斯更新

reason.zh: 第 6 章：站在雇主那边看，看到信号后修正对求职者类型的判断，就是一次贝叶斯更新。
reason.en: Chapter 6: from the employer’s side, revising a belief about the applicant’s type after seeing the signal is a Bayesian update.

reason.zh: 第 6 章：做回头客生意的店今天卖一辆柠檬，明天就没人上门；这是把一次性的囚徒困境变成重复博弈。
reason.en: Chapter 6: a shop living on repeat customers loses them by selling a lemon today; reputation turns a one-shot prisoner’s dilemma into a repeated game.

reason.zh: 第 7 章：合同只能写在看得见的结果上，于是总在“让代理人多承担结果”和“给他保险”之间取舍，并链到《稀缺会搬家》的激励。
reason.en: Chapter 7: contracts can only be written on outcomes, so they trade off making the agent bear the result against insuring him; it links incentives in scarcity-moves.

reason.zh: 第 7 章：最优的自付比例在中间，这是保险几乎都有免赔额的第二个原因，第一个是第 5 章的筛选。
reason.en: Chapter 7: the best co-pay is in between, the second reason nearly every policy has a deductible; the first is chapter 5’s screening.

label.en: The other side of deposit insurance

reason.zh: 第 7 章：存款保险是教科书里的另一个例子，存款人不再担心银行，也就不再盯着银行冒险，并链到《钱是从哪里来的》第 3 章。
reason.en: Chapter 7: deposit insurance is the other textbook case; depositors stop worrying and stop watching the bank’s risks; it links where-money-comes-from chapter 3.

label.zh: 利率赶走稳当的借款人

reason.zh: 第 8 章把柠檬的道理搬到借钱上：利率一高，稳当的借款人先不借了，留下的平均更危险，所以银行宁可不涨利率。
reason.en: Chapter 8 moves the lemons logic to lending: a higher rate drives safe borrowers away first and leaves riskier ones, so the bank prefers not to raise it.

reason.zh: 第 8 章提到斯蒂格利茨和韦斯也讨论了“借了钱就去冒更大的险”这另一半道德风险。
reason.en: Chapter 8 notes that Stiglitz and Weiss also treat the other half, moral hazard: borrowers taking bigger risks once funded.

label.en: The rate is the price of time

reason.zh: 第 8 章问银行为什么不用利率这个价格来出清，并链到《钱是从哪里来的》第 6 章讲利率为什么是时间的价格。
reason.en: Chapter 8 asks why banks do not clear the market with the rate, and links where-money-comes-from chapter 6 on why interest is the price of time.

reason.zh: 第 9 章：信用分把“以前怎么还钱”压缩成一个数，让银行能把第 8 章混在一起的借款人分开定价。
reason.en: Chapter 9: a credit score compresses past repayment into one number, letting banks price separately the borrowers chapter 8 had to pool.

reason.zh: 第 9 章：分数只是排序，门槛是银行的选择；拖动门槛，漏掉的坏人和误伤的好人此消彼长，和信号检测论的门槛是一回事。
reason.en: Chapter 9: the score only ranks; the cutoff is the bank’s choice, trading missed bad borrowers against rejected good ones, the same threshold as in signal detection.

reason.zh: 第 9 章：坏账本来就少，被拒的人里大多数其实会还钱，这是基础率的作用，并链到《数字没有说谎》。
reason.en: Chapter 9: defaults are rare, so most rejected applicants would have repaid; that is the base rate at work, and it links numbers-lie.

reason.zh: 第 9 章说一个分数能告诉你多少还取决于基础率，并链到贝叶斯诊断一课：和检测阳性的预测值是同一个计算。
reason.en: Chapter 9 says what a score tells you also depends on the base rate and links the Bayes diagnostics lesson: the same calculation as a test’s positive predictive value.

label.en: When the score becomes the target

reason.zh: 第 9 章：有人为了降低负债率在报告日前还款；分数一旦成了目标，就不再那么好地测量原本要测的东西。
reason.en: Chapter 9: people repay before the reporting date to lower utilisation; once the score is a target it measures less well what it was built to measure.

label.en: The clearer the view, the harder the spiral

reason.zh: 第 10 章：数据越多，第 3–4 章的螺旋越难转起来；可看得越清，最右边那一档就越可能被挤出市场。
reason.en: Chapter 10: more data makes chapters 3–4’s spiral harder to start, but the clearer the view, the more the riskiest class may be priced out.
